newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 4.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.

- The Irish Prime Minister, John Bruton has belatedly joined other leaders in parliament to appeal to Dunnes Stores to make the Price Waterhouse report publicly available following the resignation of one of his ministers over alleged irregular payments.
- The Department of Agriculture on Tuesday announced five new cases of BSE.

- The multi-party talks on Northern Ireland were on Tuesday adjourned until next week with the chairman, George Mitchell indicating that if there is no agreement on decommissioning of arms he may put forward his own proposals on the issue.

- The leader of the opposition Fianna Fail, Bertie Ahern, has warned that any member of his parliamentary party involved in the Dunnes Stores controversy on irregular payments will be immediately expelled and cannot seek re-election.
- The government's finances are much healthier than expected, showing a surplus of 153 million Irish pounds for the 11 months to the end of November.
- Dunnes stores will open its controversial Price Waterhouse report to the Revenue Commissioners after the resignation of a government minister over alleged irregular payments from the company.
- Proposals to copperfasten in law a "religious veto" over teacher appointments have been dropped from a forthcoming Education Bill.
- Justice Minister Nora Owen said on Tuesday she needed 21 million Irish pounds extra to fund her department this year because of a series of unexpected costs.
- The profit margin of Irish-owned manufacturing companies dropped from 4.4 percent in 1991 to 4.0 percent three years later despite benefits of strong economic growth in the interim.
